  "extractions": [

      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F000"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [
          "F002",
          "F003",
          "F004"
        ],
        "choice_quote": "F001:F004",
        "choice_text": "An eligible employee must satisfy all three criteria: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",
        "logic_quote": "F002:F004",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.801",
          "§ 825.105(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005:F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F006"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110.",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F001:F002"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (b)(2)"
        ],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, and, subject to the exceptions in paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F007",
          "F008",
          "F009"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement (including a collective bargaining agreement) exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F006"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [
          "F008",
          "F009"
        ],
        "choice_quote": "F007:F009",
        "choice_text": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted if either condition is met: (i) the break was occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break.",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": [
          "USERRA",
          "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."
        ],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F008"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, when there is absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F008",
        "references": [
          "USERRA",
          "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."
        ],
        "statement": "The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F010"
        ],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (such as sick or vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits), the week counts as a week of employment; and for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F006",
          "F007"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F011"
        ],
        "scope_text": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F012"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110 and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (c)(2)",
          "§ 825.801",
          "29 CFR part 785",
          "FLSA"
        ],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110 and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work, where the determining factor is the number of hours worked within the meaning of the FLSA, and the determination is not limited by methods of recordkeeping or by inaccurate compensation agreements."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F012"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "FLSA"
        ],
        "statement": "Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F013"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": [
          "USERRA",
          "§ 825.801(c)"
        ],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, and a person reemployed following USERRA-covered service has those hours added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F013"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "can generally",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": [
          "USERRA",
          "§ 825.801(c)"
        ],
        "statement": "The employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations in order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F014"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA hours-worked recordkeeping requirements.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": [
          "FLSA",
          "29 CFR part 541",
          "§ 825.102",
          "§ 825.801(d)"
        ],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including for FLSA recordkeeping-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.300(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F015"
        ],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave."
      }
    }
  ]

unit_attributes.choice_text: An eligible employee must satisfy all three criteria: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, and, subject to the exceptions in paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement (including a collective bargaining agreement) exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted if either condition is met: (i) the break was occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, when there is absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (such as sick or vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits), the week counts as a week of employment; and for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months.
Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110 and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110 and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work, where the determining factor is the number of hours worked within the meaning of the FLSA, and the determination is not limited by methods of recordkeeping or by inaccurate compensation agreements.
Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, and a person reemployed following USERRA-covered service has those hours added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations in order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA hours-worked recordkeeping requirements.
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including for FLSA recordkeeping-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave.

The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave.
